subject: AvaCloud renewal: usage breakdown, surge mitigation & proposed term amendment
messages:
From: Jenna Morales <jenna@avacloud.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@avacloud.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal coming up — we've seen a big mid-quarter spike

Hi Ethan,

Quick note — our renewal with Redwood is coming up in January and we’ve noticed a material spike in token consumption over the last 6 weeks tied to a new recommendation feature. We don't have the full breakdown on our side yet, but our billing contact asked if you can share a usage-by-route export and any latency/timeout anomalies you surfaced.

Two asks:
- Can you send the last 90 days of per-endpoint token consumption (csv) and the 95th percentile latency snapshot?
- What are our options for handling short-term surges without committing to a much higher baseline?

We want to avoid surprises when the renewal hits. Looping in procurement for visibility.

Thanks,
Jenna
Jenna Morales
Head of Platform, AvaCloud
jenna@avacloud.ai

Attachment: N/A
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Morales <jenna@avacloud.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@avacloud.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — we've seen a big mid-quarter spike

Hi Jenna — thanks for the heads up.

I pulled together the per-route export (attached) and a short latency snapshot from our Console for the same window. Highlights up front:
- 45% of the incremental spend is from the new recommendations endpoint (/v1/recs) when run with n=5 logits sampling.
- Median latency unchanged (~85ms); 95th moved from 230ms to ~310ms during peak windows (late UTC business hours).
- We saw several 500-level retries at the same time as the spike which our runtime team flagged as transient KV cache pressure.

Options to handle surges without a permanent baseline increase:
1) Temporary burst credits (one-time top-up) — good for spiky weeks.
2) Short-term staged commit (60–90 day uplift) with automatic rollback to baseline after usage normalizes.
3) Route-level rate limiting + prefix caching to reduce repeat tokens (our Optimize team can run a quick eval).

I attached: ava_usage_dec_to_nov_q4.csv and latency_dashboard_dec.png. Laura — looping you for the proposed mitigation and pricing MOP.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call next week to align mitigation + procurement path. Are you available Tue/Wed?

Best,
Ethan Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ethan_park@redwood.ai
Attachments: ava_usage_dec_to_nov_q4.csv (csv), latency_dashboard_dec.png (png)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Jenna Morales <jenna@avacloud.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Dec 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — we've seen a big mid-quarter spike

Team — quick internal note then I'll join the call.

Root cause (runtime): KV cache fragmentation under concurrent recommendation batches + a configuration that kept n_context higher than needed for that route. Ops fix is low-risk (cache shard rebalance + knob to cap n_context per-route). That should bring 95th back to ~240ms.

Commercial options we recommend to Jenna:
- Option A (short-term surge): One-time 500k burst credits at current rate to smooth December; no term change.
- Option B (commit flex): 90-day 20% uplift to existing commit (credit applied immediately) + an explicit 10% surge buffer priced at a discounted unit rate; converts to baseline only with confirmation.
- Option C (term amendment + uplift): 18-month term extension, 30% commit increase, deeper per-unit discount and dedicated throughput lanes during known monthly peaks.

I'll prepare a pricing MOP and a short ROI worksheet comparing Option A/B/C. Monica — can you draft the MOP (pricing_mop_v2.pdf) and include DocuSign-friendly language for the 90-day uplift?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
Attachments: N/A
From: Jenna Morales <jenna@avacloud.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — we've seen a big mid-quarter spike

Thanks for the quick analysis. A couple of clarifying Qs before the call:
- For Option B (90-day uplift) — how does the automatic rollback work? Is it purely usage-based and reversed on the bill, or is there a manual sign-off?
- If we take Option A plus some route-level rate limiting, roughly what percent reduction in tokens could we expect for the recommendations endpoint?

We’re trying to keep procurement timelines tight (Jan renewal), so if there’s a clean 90-day path that's reversible, that would be preferred.

-Jenna

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, procurement@avacloud.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Dec 2027 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal proposal: ROI recap and recommended path (Option B preferred)

Hi Jenna — following our call today, attached is the ROI summary and the proposed MOP. TL;DR and ask below.

ROI highlights:
- Baseline: current commit covers ~85% of average monthly consumption.
- Spike window projected to add ~1.2–1.6M tokens/month over 90 days (recommendations route).
- Option B (recommended): 90-day 20% uplift to commit (applied immediately), plus a 10% surge buffer at 40% discounted unit rate. Estimated incremental cost over 90 days: $14.2k. Estimated avoided overage/latency cost + engineering ops = $22k+ (based on historical incidents). Net estimated benefit: ~$7.8k.

Mechanics for rollback: the uplift is implemented as a time-bound amendment in HubSpot/DocuSign that auto-expires after 90 days. If actual usage remains within 105% of the pre-uplift baseline for two consecutive 30-day windows at the end of the term, the uplift will not convert to baseline and billing will be reconciled (credits applied). We include an explicit manual opt-in if you want to convert early.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_mop_v2.pdf (DocuSign ready), ava_usage_dec_to_nov_q4.csv, latency_dashboard_dec.png

Next steps requested:
1) Confirm Option B in email so I can issue the 90-day amendment via DocuSign.
2) Provide procurement contact to push DocuSign.
3) Ops will schedule a kernel/config change to reduce n_context for /v1/recs within 48 hours of confirmation.

Happy to hop on a 15m call to walk the MOP.

Best,
Ethan Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_pricing_mop_v2.pdf

Ethan — we’ll take Option B. Procurement contact for DocuSign is procurement@avacloud.ai (Marcel Ruiz). Please send the amendment and I’ll route it.

Also appreciate the clear rollback language. Can you confirm the target date for the ops change (n_context cap) and whether that requires a maintenance window? If it's hotfix-level, we can approve.

Thanks — Jenna
